experiment_description: Central concept: fabricate an air-isolated vertical van der Waals device in which a target monolayer CrI3 magnetic layer is placed between hBN dielectric layers and graphene/graphite electrodes so that an out-of-plane voltage can both break inversion symmetry, generating Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, and electrostatically dope CrI3, tuning magnetic anisotropy for voltage-controlled topological spin textures. The fabrication procedure starts from bulk CrI3 crystals synthesized by chemical vapor transport from elemental Cr and I precursors with Cr:I molar ratio 1:3; precursor grade and furnace temperature profile are not specified in the provided text. Inside a nitrogen-filled inert glovebox, CrI3, hBN, and graphene/graphite flakes are mechanically exfoliated using PDMS films. Exfoliated hBN, CrI3, and graphene/graphite flakes are sequentially transferred onto pre-patterned Au electrodes on a 285-nm SiO2/Si substrate to form a graphene/graphite–hBN–CrI3–hBN/graphene vertical heterostructure. The reported dielectric hBN layer used for electrostatic gating has thickness 9.8 nm, and the CrI3 monolayer thickness used in device modeling is 0.7 nm. The device is loaded in situ from the glovebox into an optical cryostat for magneto-optical-electric measurements, with CrI3 kept isolated from ambient atmosphere during fabrication and measurement. Optical micrograph inspection and subsequent magneto-optical/Raman characterization are used to determine whether the intended active heterostructure geometry is formed; the exact lateral area, yield over multiple fabricated devices, and edge-to-active-region distances are not reported.

target_air_isolated_gated_monolayer_cri3.description: Whether the inert-atmosphere exfoliation and transfer process produced the intended air-isolated gated monolayer CrI3 heterostructure for magneto-optical-electric measurements.

experiment_description: Central concept: quantify the hBN dielectric response used to convert applied voltage in the monolayer CrI3 vertical device into out-of-plane electric field and electrostatic doping, which are the control knobs for voltage-tunable DMI and magnetic anisotropy. The hBN dielectric layer is part of a graphene–hBN–CrI3–graphene/graphite device stack on SiO2/Si. Its thickness is determined by optical contrast on an hBN–SiO2–Si structure: white light is normally incident and focused with a 50×, NA = 0.45 microscope objective, reflected light is collected through a beamsplitter into a spectrometer, and a CCD records the spectrally resolved reflected signal. The optical contrast is defined as C = (R_SiO2 − R_SiO2+hBN)/R_SiO2, where R_SiO2 is the normal-incidence reflection coefficient of bare SiO2/Si and R_SiO2+hBN is the coefficient for hBN-covered SiO2/Si. The relative dielectric constant of the hBN dielectric is measured using a ferroelectric analyzer; electrode geometry, AC amplitude, and frequency are not specified in the provided text. The spatial scope is the dielectric flake used in the gated device; the exact mapped area and number of measurement points are not reported.

hbn_relative_dielectric_constant.description: The measured relative dielectric constant of the hBN dielectric layer used in the gated monolayer CrI3 device.

experiment_description: Central concept: verify that the active CrI3 flake in the voltage-controlled topological-spin-texture device is in the monolayer magnetic limit by probing spin-lattice-coupled Raman modes. Polarization-resolved and temperature-dependent Raman measurements are performed on the active CrI3 region of the hBN-encapsulated/gated device using a Witec Alpha 300R Plus low-wavenumber confocal Raman microscope integrated with a closed-cycle He optical cryostat and superconducting magnet. Excitation is a 633 nm laser with approximately 0.3 mW power. A 50× objective with NA = 0.45 is used at cryogenic temperature and under magnetic-field-compatible conditions. Raman signals are collected through a photonic crystal fiber into a spectrometer with an 1800 g/mm grating. Cross-polarized (XY) and co-linear (XX) configurations are obtained by rotating an analyzer before the fiber. Typical integration time is 120 s. Temperature is swept across the low-temperature ferromagnetic regime and above the magnetic ordering range while monitoring the same confocal spot or designated active region; the exact lateral spot size, active-area dimensions, and number of independent positions are not reported. The measurement targets the Raman-active phonon selection and its temperature-dependent coupling to magnetic order in monolayer CrI3.

a1g_raman_phonon_frequency_cm_minus1.description: The measured Raman shift of the A1g phonon mode used for monolayer CrI3 identification.

raman_spin_lattice_coupling_onset_temper.description: The temperature scale at which the polarization-resolved Raman response changes due to spin-lattice coupling in the CrI3 monolayer.

a1g_raman_polarization_channels.description: The polarization channels in which the A1g Raman phonon is detected for the monolayer CrI3 device.

experiment_description: Central concept: establish the baseline magnetic state of the target monolayer CrI3 device before applying voltage-induced DMI/anisotropy control, so that later anomalous circular-dichroism features can be assigned to voltage-created topological spin textures rather than ordinary ferromagnetic hysteresis. Polar reflective magnetic circular dichroism (RMCD) is measured on a designated region of the monolayer CrI3 device using a magneto-optical-electric joint-measurement scanning imaging system based on a Witec Alpha 300R Plus confocal platform, a closed-cycle superconducting magnet with up to 7 T field capability, and a cryogen-free optical cryostat with 10 K base temperature. A 633 nm laser with fixed power about 3 µW is modulated by a photoelastic modulator at 50 kHz, reflected from a non-polarizing beamsplitter with R/T = 30/70, and focused onto the active CrI3 region using a 50× objective with NA = 0.55. The reflected beam is collected by the same objective and detected by a photomultiplier tube coupled to a lock-in amplifier. The device gate voltage is fixed at 0 V. Out-of-plane magnetic field µ0H is swept in both directions through the low-field switching region, and high-field RMCD response is also checked to test for interlayer antiferromagnetic signatures. Temperature-dependent RMCD is acquired on the same device region to determine the magnetic ordering temperature. The confocal spot is positioned within the active region; the exact illuminated area, distance from edges, and number of spatial positions are not reported.

zero_gate_coercive_field_T.description: The coercive out-of-plane magnetic field of the monolayer CrI3 device measured by RMCD at zero gate voltage.

zero_gate_curie_temperature_K.description: The Curie temperature of the monolayer CrI3 device measured by temperature-dependent RMCD at zero gate voltage.

high_field_rmcd_step_present_zero_gate.description: Whether the zero-gate RMCD loop contains a high-field step associated with interlayer antiferromagnetic coupling.

experiment_description: Central concept: test voltage creation and continuous manipulation of topological spin textures in the strict monolayer CrI3 limit by using reflective topological circular dichroism, an optical-frequency analogue of the topological Hall effect. The same air-isolated gated monolayer CrI3/hBN/graphene device is measured at 10 K with the polar RMCD setup: 633 nm laser, approximately 3 µW power, 50 kHz photoelastic modulation, non-polarizing R/T = 30/70 beamsplitter, 50× NA = 0.55 objective, photomultiplier detection, lock-in readout, superconducting out-of-plane magnetic field, and a voltage source meter connected to the vertical electrodes. Gate voltage Vg is swept over the positive electron-doping range from 0 V to about 16 V, with representative loops at 0, 8, 12, and 16 V and phase maps over approximately 0–15/16 V. Out-of-plane magnetic field µ0H is swept over the switching/topological range in both directions, approximately within ±0.2 T in the plotted maps. The total RMCD signal is decomposed as I_RMCD = I_RCD(M) + I_RCD(T), where I_RCD(M) is the conventional reflective circular dichroism component proportional to the out-of-plane ferromagnetic magnetization background and I_RCD(T) is the topological circular dichroism component proportional to topological charge density; I_RCD(T) is obtained by subtracting the conventional magnetic background from total RMCD. RCDT peak positions are extracted by Gaussian fitting and plotted versus gate voltage. The measurement is made on a designated confocal spot/active region of the device; exact lateral spot diameter, spatial map area, and number of independent devices or positions are not reported. The phase-mapping objective is to determine the voltage range in which nontrivial topological magnetic order is optically detected and how its characteristic field shifts with voltage as magnetic anisotropy evolves from perpendicular toward in-plane.

topological_circular_dichroism_onset_vol.description: The gate voltage at which the RCDT signal first emerges from the near-zero background in the voltage-dependent RMCD phase diagram.

type_i_to_type_ii_skyrmion_transition_vo.description: The gate voltage at which the voltage-dependent RCDT response changes between the low-voltage topological regime associated with perpendicular anisotropy and the high-voltage regime associated with small in-plane anisotropy.

positive_topological_charge_peak_field_s.description: The fitted slope of the magnetic-field position of the RCDT peak associated with positive topological charge as a function of gate voltage in the linear voltage-tuning regime.

negative_topological_charge_peak_field_s.description: The fitted slope of the magnetic-field position of the RCDT peak associated with negative topological charge as a function of gate voltage in the linear voltage-tuning regime.

conventional_rcdm_hysteresis_present_at_.description: Whether a residual conventional ferromagnetic RCDM hysteresis component remains in the RMCD loop under the high positive gate-voltage condition.

voltage_induced_topological_phase_sequen.description: The sequence of magnetic phases inferred from voltage-dependent RMCD/RCDT under the positive-gate sweep.

experiment_description: Central concept: characterize the thermal stability and field-temperature phase boundaries of voltage-induced two-dimensional topological spin textures in monolayer CrI3 under a gate condition that drives the system into the high-voltage, small-in-plane-anisotropy regime. The gated monolayer CrI3 device is biased at +16 V and measured by polar RMCD/RCDT using the same optical configuration: 633 nm laser, about 3 µW power, 50 kHz PEM modulation, 50× NA = 0.55 objective, PMT and lock-in detection, closed-cycle cryostat, and superconducting out-of-plane magnetic field. RMCD loops are collected at discrete temperatures including 10, 15, 18, 21, 24, and 27 K, and field-temperature maps are acquired over roughly 10–27 K while sweeping µ0H in both directions across approximately ±0.2 T. Positive-to-negative and negative-to-positive field-sweep directions are recorded separately to distinguish opposite topological-charge signs. RMCD peak positions and half-peak widths are obtained by Gaussian fitting; peak positions are plotted versus temperature. Temperature cuts of RMCD are also taken at selected fixed out-of-plane fields including approximately ±0.02, ±0.03, ±0.035, and ±0.04 T to identify the field-dependent transition temperature. The measurement is performed on the same designated active monolayer region; exact illuminated area, number of spatial positions, and device-to-device statistics are not reported. The objective is to determine how temperature and magnetic field bound the topological magnetic phase produced by voltage-controlled spin-orbit interactions.

topological_to_in_plane_ferromagnetic_tr.description: The temperature at which the topological magnetic phase gives way to the in-plane ferromagnetic state under +16 V gate bias.

in_plane_ferromagnetic_to_paramagnetic_t.description: The temperature at which the in-plane ferromagnetic state gives way to the paramagnetic state under +16 V gate bias.

positive_topological_peak_field_temperat.description: The fitted magnitude of the temperature dependence of the magnetic-field position of the RMCD/RCDT peak associated with positive topological charge under +16 V bias.

negative_topological_peak_field_temperat.description: The fitted magnitude of the temperature dependence of the magnetic-field position of the RMCD/RCDT peak associated with negative topological charge under +16 V bias.

topological_phase_critical_temperature_a.description: The critical temperature for the topological magnetic phase under +16 V bias at an out-of-plane magnetic-field magnitude of 0.04 T.
The critical temperature for the topological magnetic phase under +16 V bias at an out-of-plane magnetic-field magnitude of 0.02 T.
